blocks.title: How to read this report
blocks.intro: This is not a test with right or wrong answers. It shows what your answers say about you and what that could mean for your future. Treat it as advice, not a rule: nothing here is set in stone, and no single career or field is the only right choice. One field of study can lead to many different careers.

items.title: Investment Banker
items.summary: Your top interests in Enterprising, Conventional, and Investigative suggest you would thrive in a role that combines leadership, detailed organization, and complex problem-solving. Your strong drive for Wealth, Reputation, and Status, along with a preference for fast-paced, large organizations, aligns well with investment banking.
items.market: This field generally offers significant growth opportunities and financial rewards for those who demonstrate high performance.
items.takesLabel: WHAT IT TAKES TO GET THERE
items.takes: The main steps to enter this field involve gaining a strong understanding of finance and business through formal education, along with practical experience.
items.now: You could begin by taking a free online course on financial markets or investment fundamentals to explore your interest further.
items.aiTitle: How AI may change this career
tasks: Routine market research and report generation
evidence: Global evidence: Globally, AI tools are automating many routine data analysis and report generation tasks in finance, allowing professionals to spend more time on client interaction, strategic advice, and complex problem-solving, based on general industry trends.

In your market: AI adoption in financial services in the GCC is generally growing, particularly in areas like data analysis and back-office operations, but strong human relationships and cultural understanding remain key in this market.
skills: Client relationship management and trust-building
Complex negotiation and deal structuring
Strategic advisory for unique business challenges
Ethical decision-making and risk assessment
Understanding market nuances and human behavior
items.means: As a career changer with no work experience, understanding how AI assists with data analysis is important. You could consider taking a free online course in basic financial data analysis tools to see how they work alongside human expertise.

items.title: Lawyer

Your strengths in Strategic thinking, Communication, and Learning, along with values like Impact and Reputation, are well-suited for a legal career.

items.takesLabel: WHAT IT TAKES TO GET THERE
items.takes: Becoming a lawyer typically requires completing a university degree in law and passing professional examinations to be licensed.
items.now: It would be helpful to research different areas of law and perhaps watch free online lectures or webinars that introduce legal concepts.
items.aiTitle: How AI may change this career
evidence: Global evidence: Globally, AI assists lawyers by speeding up legal research and document analysis, freeing up time for higher-level strategic work, complex client interaction, and nuanced legal advice, based on general industry trends.

In your market: Legal firms in the GCC are increasingly using AI for efficiency in tasks like research, but the demand for skilled lawyers who can provide nuanced advice, build client trust, and represent clients effectively remains strong.
skills: Strategic thinking and complex problem-solving
Court advocacy and persuasive argumentation
Client counseling and empathetic listening
Ethical judgment and navigating legal ambiguities
Negotiating complex settlements and advising on human impact
items.means: Even without legal experience, understanding how AI tools help with legal research is useful. You could explore free online introductions to legal research principles and how technology aids this process.

blocks.t: One small step for this week, then a simple 90-day path, built around your top career match
Built around your top match: Investment Banker
Your first step this week

A good first step is to identify two specific job titles from your matched careers list that involve working closely with people, such as a Life Coach or a Career Counselor. Then, find two or three people currently working in each of those roles in Saudi Arabia or another GCC country using a professional networking site like LinkedIn. Why: This will help you understand the day-to-day work and real-life experiences of people in these roles, which is helpful given your interest in Relationships and Communication.
YOU WILL PRODUCE
A short list of 4-6 potential contacts (names and their current job titles) you could reach out to.
WHEN
Within 2 days, about 1 hour
Worksheet:
Days 2–7

Days 2-3 — We suggest writing a short, polite message (2-3 sentences) to send to each of the people on your list from Day 1. Ask if they would be open to a brief 15-minute online chat about their career path. You will produce: Two draft messages, one for each career title, ready to send.
Day 4 — You could send the messages you drafted on Days 2-3 to the people you identified. You will produce: Messages sent, and a note of who you contacted.

Days 5-6 — If someone responds, we advise you to prepare 3-4 simple questions you would like to ask them about their work, for example, "What does a typical day look like?" or "What parts of your job do you enjoy most?" You will produce: A list of 3-4 questions for an informational chat.

Day 7 — A good way to end the week is to review what you produced and pick the next step. This could be scheduling a chat if someone replied, or looking for more people to contact if you didn't hear back. You will produce: A clear next action item for the following week, based on your progress.
Your next 90 days
Weeks 2–4 — Build momentum It would help to complete at least two 15-minute online chats with people in roles like Life Coach, Career Counselor, or Real Estate Agent.

You could consider finding a free, short online course that introduces basic concepts related to one of the careers that interested you most from your conversations, such as 'introduction to coaching' or 'basics of real estate'.

A good next step would be to compare the skills needed for a Real Estate Agent and a Lawyer by looking at 3-4 job descriptions for each in Saudi Arabia, noting common skills like 'communication' or 'negotiation'.

Months 2–3 — Build Taking a slightly longer online course in a specific skill relevant to Investment Banker or Military Officer roles, such as financial modeling basics or project management fundamentals, is recommended.

We advise you to identify a local professional organization or group related to one of your matched careers (e.g., finance professionals, legal associations, or coaching circles) in the GCC and explore if they offer virtual events or resources.

You could prepare a basic resume highlighting your communication, leadership, and relationship-building strengths, thinking about how these skills apply to roles like a Sports Coach or Military Officer, even without direct work experience.
Your skills to build and practice exercise: Investment Banker
SKILLS TO BUILD

Data Interpretation and Contextual Understanding — AI tools can process vast amounts of financial data, but a human touch is still needed to truly understand what the numbers mean for a business or market and to place them in a broader context.

Ethical Judgment and Stakeholder Consideration — Financial decisions often have major impacts on many people, and while AI can analyze outcomes, deciding what is right, fair, and best for all involved still requires human ethics and good judgment.
PRACTICE EXERCISE

A good exercise would be to find a simple, publicly available annual report summary from a company you find interesting (you can search online for 'company X annual report summary'). Ask a free AI tool to list 3-5 key financial trends or risks from this summary. Then, read the summary yourself and compare the AI's points with what you understood. Note down any important details or 'human context' you found that the AI might have missed, or any ethical implications of the company's activities that AI did not highlight.
YOU WILL HAVE
You will have a document with the AI's summary, your own notes on additional insights or contextual details, and your thoughts on any ethical considerations related to the company's activities.

Your strengths in building relationships, clear communication, and leadership are excellent foundations for a new career, even without prior work experience. A path like becoming a Real Estate Agent could allow you to use these skills to guide clients and build a trusted professional reputation in the GCC market.
It would help to complete a licensed real estate training program in Saudi Arabia or another GCC country.
These programs teach you about property laws and market practices.
You could consider joining a well-known real estate agency as a trainee or junior agent. This would allow you to gain practical experience and learn from others.
A good next step would be to build your network by connecting with developers, property owners, and other real estate professionals in the region. Strong relationships are important in this field.

intro: Courses that build the skills your matched careers need. These are for later: use them as a guide when you are ready, not something to do all at once.

items.title: Financial Modeling & Valuation Analyst (FMVA)
items.about: What it is about: This certification covers financial modeling, Excel skills, discount cash flow (DCF) methods, and valuation techniques.
items.why: Learning financial modeling and valuation is directly useful for an investment banker to analyze companies and advise clients.

items.title: Islamic Finance and Banking
items.about: What it is about: This course teaches the basic ideas of banking and financial tools that follow Shariah law.
items.why: Understanding Islamic finance principles is very important for an investment banker working in Saudi Arabia.

items.title: Emotional Intelligence
items.about: What it is about: This course helps you develop self-awareness, empathy, and skills for managing relationships.
items.why: Emotional intelligence is a core skill for a sports coach to understand and motivate athletes and to manage team relationships effectively.

items.title: Real Estate Finance and Investment
items.about: What it is about: This course explores how to value, finance, and analyze investments in real estate.
items.why: Understanding how to value properties and the financial side of real estate is a core part of advising clients as a real estate agent.

items.title: Negotiation Mastery
items.about: What it is about: This course provides practical ways to negotiate and resolve disagreements.
items.why: A real estate agent often negotiates deals between buyers and sellers, so improving negotiation skills would be very helpful.

items.title: Contract Law
items.about: What it is about: This course covers the main ideas of how contracts are made, enforced, and what happens if they are broken.
items.why: Understanding contract law is a fundamental skill for a lawyer, as many legal tasks involve creating or dealing with contracts.
